_comment: Hand-written raw-spec.json (the shape extract.lua dumps), used by checks.resolve-lazy-self.
#49: lazy.nvim listed in the spec with a `tag`, `build`, and `dependencies` -- the
reserve-name-and-merge path (see raw-spec-collide.json for the collision path instead).
`build` is a `kind ~= "none"` value on purpose: it is recorded nowhere in lazyNvim
(build/dependencies are dropped entirely for lazy.nvim) but does have to produce exactly one
warning saying so, and the golden `lazyNvim` entry must not carry a `build` key at all --
this fixture is the only one that can prove that (raw-spec-pin.json's `build = false` proves
the opposite: that a *deliberately disabled* build must never be warned about).
`dependencies` similarly must vanish silently: lazy already expanded it into tokyonight.nvim
as its own raw.plugins entry (this is what a real extract.lua run produces -- see the plan's
§1.5), so tokyonight.nvim is listed here too, as an ordinary plugin, and nothing is lost by
dropping the `dependencies` array itself.
Regenerate golden/tag.plugins.json and golden/tag.flake.nix with:
seed=$(nix eval --impure --raw --expr
'(builtins.getFlake (toString ./.)).inputs.lazy-nvim.outPath')
nvim -l lua/nvimx/resolve.lua tests/fixtures/lazy-self/raw-spec-tag.json \
tests/fixtures/lazy-self/golden/tag.plugins.json --lazy "$seed"
nvim -l lua/nvimx/genflake.lua tests/fixtures/lazy-self/golden/tag.plugins.json \
tests/fixtures/lazy-self/golden/tag.flake.nix
Never hand-edit the golden files.
